name: Partesnyi spiv and dukhovnyi kontsert (Ukrainian Baroque choral concerto)
lineage: Polyphonic sacred choral style of Ukrainian Orthodox church music. Partes singing, multi-voice part-writing for unaccompanied choir codified in Mykola Dyletsky's seventeenth-century Grammar of music, spread from the Kyiv and Lviv church brotherhoods into Muscovy; in the later eighteenth century it culminated in the a cappella sacred concerto of Dmytro Bortniansky, Maksym Berezovsky and Artem Vedel, trained in Hlukhiv, Kyiv and in Bortniansky's and Berezovsky's case in Italy, who joined Italianate counterpoint and dramatic contrast to Church Slavonic texts, writing for single and double choir.
